comment: Places where WeeChat's scanner (gui_color_code_size) and WeeChat's renderer
amounts of the same input. The library follows the renderer, because the
renderer is what decides what a line looks like; gui_color_code_size exists to
measure code sizes for line bookkeeping. test/oracle.test.ts asserts that every
corpus mismatch is explained by exactly one of these rules, that each rule is
still exercised, and that each example still diverges by the recorded extents.

rules.control: \x1a / \x1b followed by anything that is not \x01-\x06
rules.scanner: consumes the control plus one following character whatever it is (src/gui/gui-color.c:760-768)
rules.renderer: advances only for \x01-\x06, leaving any other character as literal text (src/gui/curses/gui-curses-window.c:940-1038)

rules.control: \x19B@ with fewer than five characters after the '@'
rules.scanner: consumes the '@' and then whatever five-character window is available (src/gui/gui-color.c:650-666)
rules.renderer: consumes the '@' only when a full five-character payload follows, otherwise stops before it (src/gui/curses/gui-curses-window.c:710-755)

rules.control: \x19*<fg>,@ or \x19*<fg>~@ with fewer than five characters after the '@'
rules.scanner: consumes the separator and the '@' unconditionally (src/gui/gui-color.c:697-715)
rules.renderer: consumes the separator, then the '@' only when a full five-character payload follows (src/gui/curses/gui-curses-window.c:824-857)
